answer: The nectar test I would run is Delegated osteopath licence with osteopathy council attestation: a licence the council renews after clinic audits, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so a licence the council renews after clinic audits stays private; the bridge is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the shale of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
